nodes.label: Safe Area
nodes.rationale: Safe areas avoid a device's interactive and display features like Dynamic Island; respecting them helps an app feel at home on the platform.

nodes.label: Audio Categories
nodes.rationale: Choose an audio category that matches how the app uses sound (e.g., Solo ambient silences other audio; Playback ignores the silence switch) to meet people's expectations.

nodes.label: Interruption Levels
nodes.rationale: Assign interruption levels that accurately represent urgency; Time Sensitive is only for events happening now or within the hour, and Critical requires an entitlement.

nodes.label: Permission Requests
nodes.rationale: Request access only to data actually needed and write purpose strings that clearly describe how and why the app collects the data.

nodes.label: Invisible Input Overlay Pattern
nodes.rationale: Native date/time inputs must be the tap target themselves because programmatic showPicker() is Chromium-only and an sr-only input inside a <button> is invalid HTML that dead-ends taps on iOS; the overlay keeps it accessible (real input + aria-label), RTL-safe, and requires no JS activation code.

nodes.label: iOS Date Picker Fix — Plan (Gates 0–3)
nodes.rationale: Both date activation paths are dead on iOS because HTMLInputElement.showPicker() is unsupported on iOS WebKit and an sr-only input nested inside a <button> is invalid HTML that swallows the tap; the invisible input overlay makes the native input the real, topmost hit target with no JS activation.

nodes.label: Scalable Text
nodes.rationale: Prioritize important content when responding to text-size changes; people increasing text size want the content they care about to be easier to read, not every word.

nodes.label: deepseek-v4-flash (broken delegation model)
nodes.rationale: Returns HTTP 401 (token expired or incorrect) when used as a delegation model; fallback is parent self-review on deepseek-v4-pro.

nodes.label: POST /auth/dev-login
nodes.rationale: Dev-only endpoint that sets an HttpOnly cookie for any seeded user by phone; used to unblock all @UseGuards(JwtCookieAuthGuard) endpoints in development.

nodes.label: 'No data shows in PWA' syndrome
nodes.rationale: Three root causes: missing .env, missing Drizzle migrations, missing auth cookie. Silent 500s (varchar vs uuid type mismatch) and dead API ports are the other main causes.

nodes.label: koralink-api systemd user service
nodes.rationale: systemd user service (with loginctl linger) chosen because background API processes started inside Hermes sessions die when the session ends; 'until pg_isready' loop used because ARM64/QEMU Postgres is slow.

nodes.label: KoraLink Post-Dev-Cycle Review
nodes.rationale: Sequenced delegation workflow: review with GLM 5.2 (slow reviewer) then fix with deepseek-v4-pro. Critical pitfall is switching delegation back to deepseek BEFORE dispatching fix sub-agents, otherwise fixes run on the wrong (slow) model.

nodes.label: KoraLink Review Workflow
nodes.rationale: Single GLM 5.2 reviewer is too slow (5+ min, sometimes stalls), so the parent agent self-reviews on deepseek-v4-pro and dispatches 4 parallel fix agents per layer, treating late GLM output as a supplementary second pass. deepseek-v4-flash cannot be used for delegation (HTTP 401).

nodes.label: KoraLink Runtime Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: Documents the runtime/infra layer between compiling code and visible data. The #1 cause of 'no data shows' is a dead API port (Hermes background processes die with the session), so a persistent systemd user service is mandated. Also records a silent-500 failure mode caused by varchar(36) IDs vs ::uuid casts in raw SQL.

nodes.label: COALESCE(BOOL_OR(...), FALSE) AS is_joined fix
nodes.rationale: The EXISTS subquery inside Drizzle db.execute was silently rejected by PostgreSQL (root cause of the empty feed); BOOL_OR reuses the existing match_players join with no extra subquery, and COALESCE handles the empty-set and unauthenticated edge cases.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE slot lock
nodes.rationale: Row-level lock prevents two hosts booking the same slot concurrently without an application-level distributed lock; only transactions targeting the same slot contend.

nodes.label: Launch Screen
nodes.rationale: A launch screen's sole function is to enhance the perception of a quick launch; it is not an artistic, branding, or advertising opportunity.

nodes.label: Splash Screen
nodes.rationale: If needed, show a beautiful graphic that succinctly communicates branding; display it at the beginning of onboarding or right after launching completes.

nodes.label: Progress Indicators
nodes.rationale: Use a determinate progress indicator when the loading duration is known and an indeterminate one when it is not.

nodes.label: Tips
nodes.rationale: Tips work best on features that are easy to describe; keep them short, actionable, and gated by eligibility rules so they reach the intended audience.

nodes.label: Tooltips
nodes.rationale: Limit tooltip content to 60-75 characters, begin with a verb, and avoid repeating the control's name because repetition rarely adds value.

nodes.label: Five UX states (loading, empty, error, populated, edge)
nodes.norm_label: five ux states (loading, empty, error, populated, edge)

nodes.label: KoraLink UI Standards
nodes.rationale: Pixel-sampled design screenshots are the design authority over tailwind.config.ts. Sampled tokens (#254132, #202124, #f7f8f7, #d4494c) supersede existing config values that were 'too dark' or 'too bright'.

nodes.label: Liquid Glass Clear Variant
nodes.rationale: Clear variant prioritizes visibility of underlying content; over bright content a ~35% dark dimming layer is required to preserve legibility.

nodes.label: Color on Liquid Glass
nodes.rationale: Apply color sparingly; for primary actions prefer coloring the background over the foreground, and only one primary action per context gets background emphasis.

nodes.label: Material Thickness Levels
nodes.rationale: Choose materials based on semantic meaning and recommended usage, not apparent color, because system settings can change a material's appearance.

nodes.label: Liquid Glass
nodes.rationale: File explicitly documents Liquid Glass design rules so the visual pattern can be replicated in any framework (Flutter, Tauri, Electron, React Native) using blur, translucency, and layered composition.

nodes.label: Attribution
nodes.rationale: Attributions express the underlying basis of a result to impart transparency; keep them factual and balance specificity so people can reason about results.

nodes.label: Calibration
nodes.rationale: Use calibration only when the feature cannot function without the initial information; collect only the most essential information and let people cancel at any time.

nodes.label: Confidence
nodes.rationale: Verify that confidence values correspond to result quality before conveying them; avoid showing low-confidence results, especially for proactive features.

nodes.label: Corrections
nodes.rationale: Provide immediate value when people correct a mistake and persist the update; prefer guided corrections over freeform ones.

nodes.label: Explicit Feedback
nodes.rationale: Request explicit feedback only when necessary and always make it voluntary; act immediately and persist the resulting changes to build trust.

nodes.label: Implicit Feedback
nodes.rationale: Always secure implicit feedback information, give people ways to restrict its flow, and prefer recent feedback to match people's changing tastes.

nodes.label: Limitations
nodes.rationale: Set realistic expectations so a limitation does not appear to be a defect; show people how to get the best results and explain why inferior results occur.

nodes.label: Mistakes
nodes.rationale: Anticipate mistakes, help people handle them, and learn from them when the learning improves the app; balance empathy with the seriousness of the consequences.

nodes.label: Multiple Options
nodes.rationale: Prefer diverse options to balance accuracy with choice, list the most likely option first, and avoid overwhelming people with too many options.
